project.title: TDD Jest Validation Gate
project.positioning: Requirement-backed tests should drive implementation; tests written only after code can mirror what was built and hide scope drift.
project.primaryCta: Use it on your next feature.
project.contributionCta: Stress-test the guardrails and contribute better prompts, checks, tests, and dashboard metrics.

introduction.title: Meet the TDD Jest Validation Gate.
introduction.purpose: Introduce the skill before naming the evidence gap it solves.
introduction.teachingPoint: The gate establishes requirement-backed Jest tests before product code.
introduction.headline: REQUIREMENT-BACKED TESTS. BEFORE PRODUCT CODE.
introduction.supportingCopy: A validation gate for keeping intent, tests, and implementation connected.

problem-hook.title: Tests written after code can mirror the code.
problem-hook.purpose: Contrast code-first generation with requirement-backed tests that drive implementation.
problem-hook.teachingPoint: When requirements define tests before product code, unmapped implementation becomes visible as drift or a potential gap instead of silently expanding scope.
problem-hook.headline: REQUIREMENTS DRIVE TESTS. TESTS DRIVE CODE.
problem-hook.supportingCopy: The gate makes the implementation boundary observable throughout the feature.

codeFirst.label: Code first
codeFirst.risk: Passing tests may only confirm the implementation that already exists.

testFirst.label: Requirement-backed TDD
testFirst.benefit: Unmapped source work surfaces as drift or a potential gap for review.

sdd-fit.title: The fourth canonical SDD phase.
sdd-fit.purpose: Place the skill between reviewed planning and implementation.
sdd-fit.teachingPoint: Jest establishes unit-level evidence before product code; engineers and Codex implement inside reviewed boundaries, and Playwright later adds complementary browser validation.
sdd-fit.headline: REVIEWED PLAN → TDD JEST → IMPLEMENT
sdd-fit.callout: Playwright complements Jest. It does not replace unit specs.

capabilities.title: A composed gate for trustworthy evidence.
capabilities.eyebrow: WHAT IT CAN DO FOR YOU
capabilities.purpose: Explain the artifacts the skill creates and the guardrails it coordinates.
capabilities.teachingPoint: The skill joins generation, baseline capture, traceability, drift, weakening, scope, and readiness checks.
capabilities.headline: FROM REVIEWED INTENT TO AUDITABLE UNIT EVIDENCE

capabilities.label: Traceability
capabilities.detail: Map requirements and acceptance IDs to standard Jest names.

capabilities.label: Drift detection
capabilities.detail: Require changed product paths to retain planned spec evidence.

capabilities.label: Weakening checks
capabilities.detail: Detect removed, skipped, todo, unmapped, or lower-assertion tests.

capabilities.label: Fixed scope
capabilities.detail: Record discoveries outside locked requirements as potential gaps.

capabilities.label: Readiness audit
capabilities.detail: Compose generation, drift, coverage, baseline, and completion evidence.

getting-started.title: Start from approved requirements in the repo.
getting-started.purpose: Show the complete preparation and approval sequence before product implementation begins.
getting-started.teachingPoint: Within reviewed feature scope, the TDD phase prepares the Unit Test Target Plan; people approve the plan and representative sample before full-suite generation and baseline capture.
getting-started.headline: REQUIREMENTS → PLAN → SAMPLE → SUITE → BASELINE → GATE

inputs.label: Requirements in the repo
inputs.detail: Product-approved feature requirements, acceptance criteria, and relevant validation cases.

inputs.label: TDD-prepared target plan
inputs.detail: Planned implementation units, source paths, spec paths, mappings, and concrete assertions.

inputs.label: Repo + NFR patterns
inputs.detail: Nearby Jest style, repository rules, shared NFRs, mocks, and fixtures.

workflow.label: Run the composed gate before product code

approval.label: Human approval before generation
approval.detail: Approve the Unit Test Target Plan and one representative failing spec before generating the complete planned suite.

red-green-refactor.title: The engineer–Codex working loop.
red-green-refactor.purpose: Show where most implementation iteration happens and why green is a checkpoint rather than a PR-ready finish line.
red-green-refactor.teachingPoint: For unit-testable behavior already in approved scope, update Jest first and confirm red before changing product code; surface genuinely new behavior as a potential gap for review.
red-green-refactor.headline: GREEN IS A CHECKPOINT. KEEP LEARNING.

canonicalMethodology.label: Canonical TDD methodology
canonicalMethodology.testList: List the desired behaviors, then choose exactly one case at a time.

cycle.definition: Turn one behavior into a runnable test and confirm it fails in the expected way.
Write just enough code for the new test and every earlier test to pass.
While all tests remain green, improve the design without changing behavior.

canonicalMethodology.repeat: Choose the next behavior from the list and repeat until the list is empty.

validatorGovernance.label: Validator evidence around the loop
validatorGovernance.statement: The validator does not redefine Red, Green, or Refactor.
validatorGovernance.boundary: Approvals, baselines, traceability, drift checks, and the composed gate are governance around TDD; they are not canonical color definitions.

workingLoop.collaboration: The engineer and Codex iterate one reviewed behavior or slice at a time.
workingLoop.greenCheckpoint: Passing Jest tests are a safe checkpoint for local exploratory testing, not proof that the feature is PR-ready.
workingLoop.localValidation: Exercise the local build to find incorrect behavior, UX defects, and edge cases that unit checks alone may not reveal.
workingLoop.inScopeChange: For a unit-testable behavior change already covered by approved requirements, update the Jest evidence first, confirm the expected failure, and then change product code.
workingLoop.outsideScopeChange: Record behavior outside approved requirements as a potential gap; do not implement it opportunistically.
workingLoop.refactor: Improve structure only while the suite remains green, then repeat until the complete reviewed slice is ready.

dashboard.title: A dashboard built for decisions.
dashboard.purpose: Frame the dashboard around engineering questions rather than volatile counts.
dashboard.teachingPoint: Headline metrics are navigation; supporting audit tables carry the decision evidence.
dashboard.headline: WHAT DO YOU NEED TO KNOW NEXT?
questions: Are reviewed plans and baselines present?
supportingViews: Initial Jest TDD suite versus final suite
dashboard.footnote: Requirement coverage is primary. Percent coverage is supporting evidence.

usage-cta.title: Use it three ways. Improve it together.
usage-cta.purpose: Give engineers immediately reusable entry points and invite contribution.
usage-cta.teachingPoint: The same gate supports standalone Codex use, direct CLI use, and orchestrated SDD.
usage-cta.headline: START WITH THE ENTRY POINT THAT FITS YOUR WORK.

usageModes.label: Standalone · Codex
usageModes.prompt: Start from the approved requirements in the repo. Prepare the Unit Test Target Plan within reviewed scope, then pause for plan and sample approval.

usageModes.label: With SDD Orchestrator
usageModes.prompt: Run SDD Orchestrator for RX-12345. Continue into the TDD Jest phase and pause for sample approval.
